cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office kettle's on strike. Help me negotiate before the clients arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've filled it twice. It still won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then water isn't its grievance. Tell it we'll stop leaving it alone after meetings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take it into the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give it my chair. I'll stand when the clients come.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads negotiation with an alleged striking kettle; A3 turns failed filling into a grievance and A5 gives up A chair to enact B meeting solution.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no boiling despite water causes A3 non-water grievance; B4 meeting offer causes A5 formal seat and standing concession.

relationship.evidence: B2 has tried repair and B4 offers helpful participation in A theory.

heightening.evidence: A5 the tea provider receives A place with clients, a practical consequence of treating it as a colleague.

specificity.evidence: A1 office, clients and kettle establish immediate need; B2 explains why ordinary water filling has not worked.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 gives a seat and takes its personal cost instead of explaining the seat-at-table metaphor.
